ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as consolidated and amended by the Law of 25 March 2020 and subsequent transpositions of EU AML Directives; Law of 13 January 2019 on the Register of Beneficial Owners (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs – RBE), amended following ECJ C-37/20; CSSF Regulation No 12-02 of 14 December 2012 on AML/CFT; Luxembourg Criminal Code Articles 505-1 et seq. on money laundering

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) of Luxembourg or equivalent foreign commercial registrar
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for states party to the Hague Convention; Consular Legalization at a Luxembourg Embassy or Consulate for non-Hague states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney granted to the person executing the SARL incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary of the country of origin or Luxembourg notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization, followed by sworn French translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copies of passports or national identity cards of all UBOs, directors and managers
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National issuing authority, certified notary, or Luxembourg Consulate
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille generally dispensed when countersigned by a notary or consular officer; otherwise Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-wealth declaration for each UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Originating licensed bank, external auditor, or regulated financial intermediary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization where required by the receiving Luxembourg notary or financial institution

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Criminal record extract / clean conduct certificate of each natural-person director or manager
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Judicial or criminal records authority of the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization, with certified French translation

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of every UBO, director, manager and authorized signatory against the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, the UN Security Council consolidated list, OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists, Luxembourg national sanctions maintained by the Ministry of Finance, and CSSF AML/CFT regulatory databases; PEP identification follows FATF 40 Recommendations and the Luxembourg statutory definition, including foreign PEPs, family members and close associates under CSSF Circular 17/650; enhanced due diligence and senior-management approval are required for any PEP or elevated-risk match; ongoing transaction monitoring and reporting obligations to the CRF (Cellule de Renseignements Financiers) apply.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), available at lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be entered in one of the working languages of the RCS (French, German or Luxembourgish) using Latin script; non-Latin text must be transliterated into Latin characters; the legal-form designator must appear as 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée' or its abbreviation 'SARL'; the name must be distinctive and not identical or confusingly similar to any existing RCS entry.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque / Bank / Kreditinstitut — requires prior CSSF banking authorization
Assurance / Insurance / Réassurance — requires prior Commissariat aux Assurances authorization
Fonds / OPC / SIF / SICAV / SICAF — requires prior CSSF authorization under Luxembourg UCI or SIF legislation
Bourse / Stock Exchange — requires prior financial-sector authorization
Avocat / Cabinet d'avocats / Barreau — reserved to members of the Luxembourg Bar
Fiduciaire — restricted if fiduciary or corporate-services activities are offered; requires compliant professional status and AML/CFT registration
État / Ministère / Administration / Luxembourg national symbols — misleading references to public authorities are prohibited
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation at the LBR is valid for 40 days and may be renewed once for an additional 40-day period if incorporation has not yet been completed; if the reserved name expires without registration, a new reservation must be filed. Where the RCS registrar rejects a name because of identity, confusing similarity, or non-compliance with naming rules, the applicant may either file a new reservation with a modified name or appeal the registrar's decision before the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg, commercial chamber, within 15 days of notification; exceptional interim-relief applications may be brought by référé.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted only through a duly regulated corporate domiciliation agent — such agents are obliged entities subject to AML/CFT registration and professional rules. The SARL must nevertheless maintain real economic substance in Luxembourg, including management functions, appropriate staff or service agreements, premises, and a Luxembourg bank account, in order to satisfy the Luxembourg Tax Administration (Administration des contributions directes) substance expectations and EU anti-abuse standards. A fully virtual shell with no physical presence or independent economic activity is not permissible for a commercial substance-sensitive trade-remedy consulting entity.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate baseline risk: approximately 5–10% annual probability of an unannounced physical inspection by the Luxembourg Tax Administration, CSSF, or social-security authorities for a low-risk consulting SARL; probability increases to 35–50% if UBO PEP/sanctions flags, incomplete substance documentation, or atypical transaction patterns are identified.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies (Loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), as amended; SARL-specific provisions under Articles 100-1 to 195-1; general provisions on companies and legal persons under Articles 1 to 89.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) maintained by the Luxembourg Ministry of Justice; incorporation is filed electronically by the authenticating notary.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial deed of incorporation (acte constitutif) and articles of association (statuts), executed before a Luxembourg notary and filed with the RCS through the LBR e-Registre channel.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital EUR 12,000, fully subscribed and fully paid in cash upon incorporation; funds must be deposited with a Luxembourg credit institution or held in the notary's segregated account until the RCS registration is effective, with a bank blocking certificate or notary attestation delivered.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: Adopted unanimously in writing by the initial shareholders on [date]. RESOLVED: the EUR 12,000 fully paid share capital, divided into 12,000 shares of EUR 1.00, is hereby subscribed and adopted. RESOLVED: the Company's registered office is fixed at [address], Luxembourg, Grand Duchy of Luxembourg. RESOLVED: the deed and articles executed before Notary [name] are ratified and the authorized corporate purpose includes trade-remedy defense consulting. RESOLVED: [name] and [name] are appointed gérants, each with sole signature authority. RESOLVED: the gérants may complete all RCS, RESA, tax, social, bank and beneficial-owner filings. This resolution is effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – online e-Registre name request portal at lbr.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name-request application to LBR for the proposed corporate name together with the legal form 'S.à r.l.' and the proposed corporate purpose. LBR will verify availability and compliance with the rule against misleading names. Upon approval, keep the reservation certificate to be referenced in the statutes.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name and legal form
Identity document of the requesting founder or proxyholder
Short description of the corporate purpose and NACE/ISIC code 7490
Power of attorney, if filed via a professional representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for conflict or likelihood of confusion, submit a ranked list of alternative names and amend the draft statutes; LBR will advise the refusal ground and a corrected application can be filed immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital deposit and bank blocking certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution or the appointed notary's segregated client account (e.g. Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État, BCEE; or a commercial bank)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary or escrow account in the name of the company being formed and deposit at least EUR 12,000 in cash. Each subscriber must transfer its share from a bank account in its own name. Obtain a capital blocking certificate (attestation de blocage) issued to the notary, which will be attached to the incorporation dossier.
required_dossiers: Passport or ID of each subscriber
Source of funds and bank reference
Draft articles with capital distribution schedule
AML/KYC forms and bank signature card
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests further AML documents, submit bank statements, transaction records, and explanation of lawful origin. If the bank refuses the account, withdraw funds and use another credit institution or deposit with the notary's client account.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of notarial incorporation deed and statutes
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg civil-law notary; Chambre des Notaires du Luxembourg
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All founders appear before the notary or are represented by a notarially appointed proxy. The notary verifies identity, legal capacity, the paid-in capital, the lawfulness of the corporate purpose, and the absence of insolvency or criminal disqualification. The founders sign the deed and statutes; the notary authenticates the signatures and retains an original for e-filing.
required_dossiers: Draft statutes and official corporate purpose
Bank capital blocking certificate
Identity documents, residence and police record extracts (casier judiciaire) for managers and shareholders with major interests
Name reservation confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies a deficiency in capital payment, capacity, or clauses, cure the defect by supplementary agreement or amend the statutes with written consent and reschedule the execution before an increased legal fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic filing at the RCS and issuance of RCS extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS); standard RCS e-filing by the notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary transmits the authenticated deed and mandatory annexes to the RCS through the LBR electronic channel. The RCS registrar confirms legal form, capital, registered office, managers, corporate purpose and identifies the beneficial owners for initial data purposes. Registration becomes legally effective upon entry in the RCS and issuance of an 'extrait de la matrice' with a Luxembourg registration number.
required_dossiers: Electronic RCS filing request
Notarial deed and full text of statutes
List of managers, powers, and joint or sole signature arrangements
Proof of full payment of capital
Initial identification of beneficial owners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS files a query, respond through the notary within 15 days with clarifications or amended annexes; if registration is suspended, rectify the particular clause and pay the administrative re-filing charge, if any.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the electronic official journal (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA) – official electronic gazette published by the Ministry of Justice through LBR
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS entry, the notary files the legal-notice text for RESA publication without delay. The publication includes the registration number, company legal form, registered office, share capital, managers and corporate object. No business activity may be relied upon against third parties before publication.
required_dossiers: RCS registration number
Certified copy of the deed
RESA filing form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If publication is delayed or erroneous, address a rectification request to LBR/RESA; the registrar orders a corrective notice and the date of first valid publication remains effective.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT and registration; Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS) for social security; common business identifier through myGuichet.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Use the RCS registration number to complete automatic tax registration where possible. For VAT, the AEDT issues a Luxembourg VAT number when the company carries out taxable supplies. The company must notify CCSS of its first employment relationship and complete the employer registration. Confirm the official accounting-reference period in the AEDT register.
required_dossiers: RCS official extract
Notarial deed
Identification of managers
Bank account details
Statement of intended taxable activity (service code ISIC 7490)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If no automatic notification is received, file the absent declarations via myGuichet with the RCS extract attached; a late filing may be regularized with a reasoned request for penalty remission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Beneficial owner declaration and corporate registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE) and internal corporate registers maintained by the managers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month of the RCS registration date, file the RBE declaration identifying natural persons who ultimately own or control more than 25% of the shares, voting rights, or exercise senior-manager control. Also create statutory corporate records: share register, transfer ledger if any, minutes of shareholders' meetings, managers' decisions and the register of registered offices. Retain these at the registered office for inspection.
required_dossiers: RBE declaration form
Passport/know-your-customer data of each beneficial owner
Ownership chart or narrative
Share register and initial capital ledger
Minutes and decision registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RBE filing is rejected or queried, correct ownership or control details, re-file within the amended deadline, and preserve evidence of the chain of control; late filings may be regularized with a waiver request to the LBR.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy – Directorate General for Industry and Crafts (Direction générale de l'industrie et de l'artisanat) and Guichet des entrepreneurs at myGuichet.lu
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement (Establishment Licence) under Article 4 of the Luxembourg Law of 2 September 2011 governing the exercise of commercial, craft and liberal-professional activities

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Luxembourg Environment Agency) – Ministry of Environment, Climate and Sustainable Development
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Not listed: office-based professional consulting activity (ISIC 7490) does not fall under Annex I or II of the amended Law of 15 May 2018 on environmental impact assessment; no environmental impact assessment or operating permit for classified installations is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: office use only; must comply with municipal sewer discharge bylaws and the Grand-Ducal Regulation on urban wastewater. Process emissions: no VOC or combustion emission points; indoor ventilation must comply with ITM occupational-hygiene standards. Waste: general waste and e-waste must be separated according to the Law of 21 March 2012 on waste management; any special waste generated through consultancy material must be handed to registered waste operators with consignment notes.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety clearance: obtain a fire-safety inspection certificate for office occupancy from the competent fire brigade and an approved bureau de contrôle (fire classification, evacuation routes, extinguishers). Structural clearance: commissioning of a certified structural surveyor to confirm the office floor load and occupancy class. Occupational clearance: Inspection du travail et des mines (ITM) workplace visit, emergency plan, first-aid equipment, and CCSS employee registration before commencement of staff operations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) – Luxembourg Income Tax Authority; registration portal: MyGuichet.lu / Gestionnaire de Tâches; VAT authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity must appoint a Luxembourg tax representative and register with the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) to obtain a business registration number; apply for a Luxembourg VAT number (numéro de TVA) with the AEDT using the RCS extract and articles of association; corporate income tax registration is effected automatically with the ACD upon RCS filing; non-resident companies with a permanent establishment or VAT-liable activities in Luxembourg must register for VAT via form 563 and obtain a 10-digit national identification number (matricule) assigned by the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (SARL is a resident company subject to Luxembourg corporate income tax (IRC) on worldwide income if managed and controlled in Luxembourg; no pass-through election available for SARL).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or partnership pass-through election for a SARL; optional joint taxation regime for qualifying family holding companies is not applicable; may elect for the special 80% participation exemption on dividend and capital gains if holding thresholds are met; can elect for VAT grouping (assujetti unique) under Article 62 VAT Law; can elect for the Luxembourg IP box regime (50% exemption of qualifying IP income); no hybrid mismatch elections available under domestic law beyond the EU ATAD-aligned anti-hybrid rules.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée – TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 0 – no general registration threshold; any taxable person supplying goods or services in Luxembourg, including foreign businesses with a fixed establishment or distance sales exceeding EU distance-selling thresholds (EUR 10,000 for cross-border B2C goods/services within the Union) or intra-Community acquisitions exceeding EUR 10,000 per year, must register for Luxembourg VAT; non-established taxable persons must register from the first taxable transaction.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance or mandatory e-invoicing for domestic B2B VAT in Luxembourg; however, all taxpayers must submit monthly/quarterly VAT returns electronically via the eCDF platform (Electronic Cash Desk of the AEDT); B2B e-invoicing is permitted under EU Directive 2014/55/EU and Peppol BIS 3.0 standards are accepted; no digital fiscal stamping or continuous transaction control (CTC) requirement; foreign taxable persons must file through the VAT One Stop Shop (OSS) for distance sales and the Reverse Charge mechanism applies to certain cross-border supplies.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods to non-EU destinations and certain supplies of services related to international trade (including services directly linked to export of goods, transportation, loading, and ancillary services) are zero-rated under Article 56 of the Luxembourg VAT Law; the supplier must retain proof of the physical departure of goods from the EU, commercial documentation evidencing the supply, and, for services, evidence that the recipient is established outside the EU and the service qualifies under the place-of-supply rules; anti-dumping trade defense consulting services are generally B2B supplies to non-resident clients, which are outside the scope of Luxembourg VAT under the general place-of-supply rule (B2B Article 44 VAT Directive) rather than zero-rated; professional consultancy related to export of goods can be zero-rated if directly linked to the export transaction and the supplier obtains written confirmation of the non-EU status of the customer.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Single Administrative Document (SAD) – Customs Export Declaration
Bill of Lading (B/L) or Air Waybill (AWB)
Proof of Exit from EU (electronic T1 or ECS statement)
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank transfer confirmation for export proceeds
Incoterm contract and proof of delivery terms
Vendor declaration of non-EU status (if services)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Misuse of zero-rating for exports triggers reassessment of VAT at 17%, plus interest at the legal rate of 3% per annum; fraudulent claims carry a criminal fine of up to EUR 100,000 and imprisonment of up to 5 years (Luxembourg General Tax Law, articles 396–398); the AEDT can impose an administrative penalty of up to 10% of the tax evaded, withhold refunds, and conduct retrospective clawbacks for up to 5 years (10 years in cases of tax fraud); taxpayers must produce export documentation on demand or face full VAT reversal and professional disqualification for trade-consulting firms.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) and the Luxembourg Ministry of Finance; foreign exchange administration is exercised under EU capital movement law with no separate Luxembourg forex control agency
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Euro is fully convertible on both capital and current account. Luxembourg applies the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union Article 63 prohibition on all capital movement restrictions within the EU, and profit remittance for SARL distributions is unrestricted once annual accounts are approved and the statutory minimum capital is unimpaired. Anti-dumping defense consulting fees are current account services, freely transferable subject only to ordinary invoice and tax reporting. There are no exchange-control approvals, pre-invoice currency authorization, or quantitative limits on dividend repatriation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No export proceeds surrender or mandatory conversion rules exist in Luxembourg. Exporters and service providers may retain all foreign currency revenues in designated accounts or convert to EUR at will. No statutory timeline for repatriation is imposed for services; only standard transfer pricing, invoicing, and anti-money-laundering transaction documentation apply. For goods exports, EU customs and VAT obligations apply, but no central bank surrender timeline exists.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account plus segregated capital structure by governance mandate
Operational Account with sub-account for client retainer escrows
Operational Account and trade finance facility for commercial LC issuance
Operational Current Account for treasury and liquidity
Capital Escrow Account for retainer trust funds

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility. Luxembourg-authorised electronic money institutions (EMIs) and payment institutions under CSSF supervision can operate cross-border via SEPA and SWIFT rails. Offshore digital EMIs not passporting under PSD/EU may not open bank accounts or provide payment services to a Luxembourg SARL without entering into a custodian-bank or agent relationship with a licensed credit institution. Pure digital EMI accounts present moderate friction for statutory anti-dumping defense work because the bank account must support high-value retainer flows, documentary evidence trails, and potentially court-ordered attachment. For non-core incidental collections, a CSSF-licensed fintech EMI account can be complementary but is not acceptable as the sole treasury rail.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a Luxembourg SARL, physical presence or a physical board meeting in Luxembourg is the default expectation for the initial KYC/AML interview. CSSF regulations and banking practice normally require the ultimate beneficial owner and authorised signatories to appear at least once in person before a bank officer, unless the bank has implemented a compliant equivalent remote video onboarding procedure approved under its internal AML/CFT framework and the EBA guidelines on remote customer onboarding. Remote opening is legally permitted only by banks that maintain a full video engagement, geolocation and electronic signature stack. Given the legal-defense business scope, banks frequently require both a physical appearance for authorised directors and submitting the anti-dumping legal advisory licence for filing.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Legal advisory classification for anti-dumping defense services: the bank may treat this as regulated legal activity requiring a Luxembourg lawyer licence or proof of appointment as a foreign-qualified trade defense counsel
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Copy of the SARL's trade-remedy consulting contract, memorandum of association with ISIC 7490 scope, the practising certificate of the engaged counsel, any Bar association registration or equivalent professional liability insurance, and a sworn declaration of the legal nature of the services.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-value cross-border retainer wires lacking adequate source-of-funds documentation, presenting a potential money laundering red flag under the Law of 12 November 2004
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed retainer agreement with clear fee schedule, client identity and ownership disclosure forms, evidence of the client's underlying trade dispute (anti-dumping proceeding reference, Customs authority case number, or UK/US counterpart), bank statements of the client showing consistent lawful business revenue, and a copy of the SARL's economic substance record confirming active trade-defense legal services.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained beneficiary and negative press exposure arising from export sanctions or Customs enforcement matters
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions screening result, definitive anti-dumping injury or proceeding documentation proving compliance work, confirmation of client's legal goods classification, and a legal opinion from a Luxembourg admitted counsel that the services do not facilitate customs evasion or dumping.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Lack of clear treasury data and inconsistent FX conversion across invoices paid in third currencies (USD, CNY, GBP)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Invoices with clearly dated FX reference, trade and services contract, SWIFT MT103 evidence for each receivable, the SARL's internal FX policy, and an audited statement or management accounts proving conversion is made at arm's-length banking rates.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For equity injections from non-EU shareholders, payment should be made via SWIFT MT103 to the SARL's EUR account at a Luxembourg bank, using beneficiary reference 'LU_SARL capital subscription'. The payment must include a plain narrative conforming to the underlying capital payment undertaking and be credited to a fully subscribed issued capital account. For EU or domestic shareholders, a TARGET2 or SEPA Credit Transfer is accepted. The bank may require a current copy of the deed of contribution, the Luxembourg notarial act of capital increase if applicable, a BCL balance-of-payments reporting via direct bank remittance form for foreign direct investment statistics, and confirmation of the economic beneficiary. The applicable harmonised balance of payments purpose code per BCL statistical regulation is 'Equity capital contribution' (portfolio or direct investment), with EBOPS/CoBA code assigned by the receiving bank.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements for anti-dumping defense fees will use SWIFT MT103 (single client credit transfer) for standard fee payments to foreign counsel, expert witnesses, customs consultants, and subcontracted legal practitioners. For high-value settlement obligations or retainer escrow disbursements, a commercial letter of credit, MT700, may be issued by the Luxembourg bank to a foreign trade defender when proof of performance is embedded (e.g., submission of a legal memorandum or receipt of a Customs event). For smaller EU disbursements, SEPA CT (ISO 20022 pain.001) will make same-day payments. Luxembourg clearing infrastructure is integrated with Target Instant Payment Settlement (TIPS) and RTGS via the TARGET2 system; no special forex surrender clearings exist.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX Forward contract (EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, EUR/CNY) with a Luxembourg-licensed credit institution
Non-deliverable forward (NDF) where cash settlement in EUR is executed for restricted-currency exposures such as CNY or INR, subject to CSSF permit classification
FX swap (swap of principal repayments or receivable conversions) for treasury liquidity management
European-style foreign currency option (purchase of EUR put / USD call) to hedge receivables from anti-dumping proceedings
Cross-currency swap (EUR/USD) for material multi-year retainer liabilities
Plain vanilla forward-rate agreement quoted by the corporate treasury desk of BIL or BGL BNP Paribas

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of annual accounts (bilan et comptes annuels) with the RCS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Societes (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months after the financial year-end (31 July for a 31 December year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing administrative penalties of EUR 100 (up to 1 month), EUR 200 (1-2 months) and EUR 500 (more than 2 months); court order to file with penalty of up to EUR 2,500; three consecutive years of non-filing may lead to administrative strike-off (radiation).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return covering corporate income tax (IRC), municipal business tax (ICC) and net wealth tax (IFL)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 31 May of the year following the tax year; ACD routinely grants extension to 31 December on request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Ex-officio assessment; late-payment interest of 0.6% per month; late-filing penalties and criminal fines for intentional omission.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT declaration (declaration annuelle en matiere de TVA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration de l'Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA (AEDT)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 10 May of the year following the calendar year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to EUR 2,500; late-payment interest of 0.6% per month; VAT liability may be assessed ex officio.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO confirmation (confirmation annuelle des beneficiaires effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre des Beneficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within one month of the anniversary of the RBE registration; any UBO change must be declared within 30 days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fine of EUR 250-1,250; until the UBO file is regularised, distributions to shareholders are blocked.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Holding of annual shareholders' meeting approving the annual accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate record under Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 (no regulatory filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of the financial year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No direct regulatory fine; late approval delays the RCS filing and triggers the RCS late-filing penalties.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent audit by a reviseur d'entreprises is mandatory where, for two consecutive financial years, the SARL exceeds at least two of the following: balance sheet total above EUR 4.4 million; net turnover above EUR 8.8 million; average workforce above 50 employees.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (LUX GAAP) under the Law of 19 December 2002 and the 10 June 2009 Grand-Ducal Regulation; IFRS as adopted by the EU is optional for separate accounts and required for certain consolidated or listed entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Each transfer of shares or change in beneficial ownership must be reported to the RBE within 30 days; an annual confirmation of the continuing accuracy of registered UBO data must be filed with the LBR within one month of the anniversary of the initial RBE registration. The articles of association must be updated where the transfer affects share classes or control rights.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Managers (gerants) and minutes of management meetings
UBO register file maintained in line with the RBE (Registre des Beneficiaires Effectifs)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,100-3,300 per year (EUR 1,000-3,000) for professional domiciliation and corporate agent services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,400-16,200 per year (EUR 5,000-15,000) for a typical small SARL statutory audit under LUX GAAP
